stem: A child with a positive Trendelenburg test due to Perthes disease in the right hip will exhibit which of the following?

options.text: The right side of the pelvis sags
The left side of the pelvis sags
The child leans backward to maintain balance
The child is unable to lift the right foot

explanation: Because the right hip is affected, the abductor muscles cannot stabilize the pelvis, causing the opposite (left) side to drop.
rationale: The test result is defined by what happens to the 'sound' side of the pelvis.

optionExplanations.A: In a positive test, the pelvis drops on the 'sound' or unaffected side when standing on the affected leg.
optionExplanations.B: Because the right hip is affected, the abductor muscles cannot stabilize the pelvis, causing the opposite (left) side to drop.
optionExplanations.C: A backward lean is more characteristic of gluteus maximus weakness, not the pelvic sag of a Trendelenburg gait.
optionExplanations.D: The test measures pelvic stability during single-leg standing on the affected side, not the ability to lift that leg.

source.hint: The test result is defined by what happens to the 'sound' side of the pelvis.
